title: How To Avoid An Increase In Misbehavior As The School Year Winds Down s-the-school-year-winds-down/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin explains why behavior commonly worsens in the final weeks of the school year—students sense summer approaching and test whether boundaries remain firm—and offers a proactive plan to prevent it. His recommendations include preemptively reaffirming the classroom management plan before any downward trend starts, presenting it as a pleasant refresher rather than an angry lecture, framing it as reassurance rather than threat, being as specific as during the first week of school, and maintaining or increasing academic pace and rigor through the final bell. He frames the goal as finishing 'not with the exhausted, salt-encrusted visage of a marathon runner, but with a sprinter's bounce'—a proactive, positive close to the year rather than a defensive scramble.
points: Behavior commonly worsens near year's end as students sense summer approaching and test whether classroom boundaries remain firm.
Preemptively reteach the classroom management plan before any downward trend begins, rather than reacting after it starts.
Present the review as a pleasant refresher and reassurance—not an angry lecture—to avoid a 'them-versus-you' dynamic.
Be as specific and thorough in the review as during the first week, rather than assuming students already remember expectations.
Maintain or increase academic pace and rigor through the final weeks; easing off invites a blasé attitude that grows misbehavior.
quotes: It’s common for behavior to worsen during the final few weeks of the school year.
Sensing summer break approaching, students begin to feel their age outpacing their grade level. They grow restless and excitable.
Knowing that a downward trending of behavior is a possibility, it’s smart to reaffirm your classroom management plan before the dip occurs.
It’s best to reteach your plan as a refresher rather than an angry response.
With testing in the review mirror, many students will conclude that the school year is essentially over, which is a surefire predictor of misbehavior.
Reach the finish line, not with the exhausted, salt-encrusted visage of a marathon runner, but with a sprinter's bounce in your step.
